title: The Chemical Industry: Fertilisers
seo_title: Grade 12 Physical Sciences: The Chemical Industry: Fertilisers Worksheets (CAPS)
standard_code: Grade 12 Physical Sciences: The chemical industry: fertilisers
standard_text: The value of fertilisers: the nutrients N, P and K; the fertiliser industry: the Haber process (ammonia), the Ostwald process (nitric acid) and the contact process (sulfuric acid); making ammonium nitrate, ammonium sulfate and phosphate fertilisers; NPK ratios; the environmental impact of fertilisers, including eutrophication. (summary of CAPS Physical Sciences, Grade 12, Chemistry: The chemical industry: fertilisers)
meta_desc: Free Grade 12 Physical Sciences worksheets (CAPS): N, P and K, the Haber, Ostwald and contact processes, ammonium salts, NPK ratios and eutrophication. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Plants need nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium.
key_sub: Ammonia is made by the Haber process.
body_html:
How to think about it

Plants need nitrogen for proteins and leaf growth, phosphorus for roots, flowers and ATP, and potassium for fruit and disease resistance. Harvesting removes these nutrients, so farmers add fertilisers. A label 3:2:1 (25) gives the ratio of N : P : K and the total percentage of nutrients.

Ammonia is made by the Haber process (N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃, iron catalyst); nitric acid by the Ostwald process; sulfuric acid by the contact process (V₂O₅ catalyst). Ammonia and these acids make ammonium nitrate and ammonium sulfate. Too much fertiliser runs off into rivers and dams and causes eutrophication.

Example

A 2 kg bag is 3:2:1 (30). Mass of nitrogen?

Nutrients = 30% of 2 kg = 600 g; N is 3/6

Answer: 300 g

Example

Which process makes sulfuric acid?

V₂O₅ catalyst

Answer: the contact process

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up the Haber and Ostwald processes.
  • Reading the NPK ratio as masses in kilograms.
  • Thinking more fertiliser always gives a bigger harvest.

faq.a: Algae grow quickly and then die; bacteria decomposing them use up the oxygen, so fish die.

faq.q: Why are fertilisers important in South Africa?
faq.a: They increase crop yields and help feed a growing population.

items.q: What is nitrogen fixation?
c: converting nitrogen gas into ammonia or nitrogen compounds that plants can use
breaking down proteins into amino acids
items.e: Done by bacteria, lightning and the Haber process.

items.q: Which processes return carbon dioxide to the atmosphere?
items.e: Volcanoes also release CO₂.

items.q: What is net production in a consumer?
c: chemical energy in food minus energy lost in faeces, urine and respiration
items.e: N = I − (F + R).

items.q: How does weathering of silicate rocks affect carbon dioxide?
c: it releases large amounts of CO₂ quickly
it removes CO₂ from the atmosphere over long timescales
it adds nitrogen to the air
items.e: Rain is slightly acidic from dissolved CO₂.

items.q: What is eutrophication?
c: excess nutrients cause algal growth, leading to low oxygen levels in water
items.e: Bacteria decomposing dead algae use up oxygen.

items.q: Which process removes carbon dioxide from the atmosphere into the biosphere?
items.e: Plants and algae fix carbon.

items.q: Why do plants need nitrogen?
c: to make proteins and chlorophyll, for leaf growth
to make strong roots and flowers only
items.e: Nitrogen is part of amino acids, proteins and chlorophyll.

items.q: Potassium for fertiliser is usually supplied as …
c: potassium nitrate made by the Haber process
items.e: Potash is mined, mostly as KCl.

items.q: Which fertiliser contains the highest percentage of nitrogen by mass?
items.e: Urea has 28 g of N in 60 g, about 47%.

items.q: The primary consumers contain 20 000 kJ m⁻² year⁻¹ and the secondary consumers contain 2 400 kJ m⁻² year⁻¹. Calculate the efficiency of energy transfer.
items.e: Efficiency = energy at next level ÷ energy at previous level × 100 = 12,0%.

items.q: Why do plants need phosphorus?
c: to make cell walls of cellulose
for root growth, flowers and fruit, and to make ATP and DNA
items.e: Phosphorus is part of ATP, DNA and cell membranes.

items.q: The producers contain 24 000 kJ m⁻² year⁻¹ and the primary consumers contain 1 920 kJ m⁻² year⁻¹. Calculate the efficiency of energy transfer.
items.e: Efficiency = energy at next level ÷ energy at previous level × 100 = 8,00%.

items.q: What is nitrogen fixation?
c: bacteria such as Rhizobium convert nitrogen gas into ammonia
items.e: Rhizobium lives in root nodules of legumes.

items.q: Which part of a living thing needs phosphorus?
c: DNA, ATP and phospholipids in membranes
items.e: Bones and teeth also contain calcium phosphate.

items.q: Which is the largest store of carbon on Earth?
items.e: The deep ocean is the largest active store.

items.q: Why do farmers need fertilisers?
c: they make the soil less acidic in all cases
plants need them for photosynthesis as an energy source
crops remove nutrients from the soil, which must be replaced
items.e: Harvesting crops removes N, P and K from the soil each season.

items.q: What is the formula of urea, a nitrogen fertiliser?
items.e: Urea is made from ammonia and carbon dioxide.

items.q: What do the letters N, P and K on a bag of fertiliser stand for?
items.e: These are the three primary nutrients plants need.

items.q: Why do plants need potassium?
c: to fix nitrogen from the air
for healthy flowers and fruit and for resistance to disease
items.e: Potassium helps with enzyme action, water balance, flowering and disease resistance.

items.q: A bag of fertiliser is labelled 3:2:1 (25). What does the 25 mean?
c: 25% of the mass of the fertiliser is the nutrients N, P and K
items.e: The number in brackets is the total percentage of N, P and K.

items.q: 4,0 mol of ethanoic acid and 4,0 mol of ethanol are mixed in 1,0 dm³. At equilibrium 1,2 mol of ethyl ethanoate has formed: CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH ⇌ CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O. Calculate K<sub>c</sub>.
items.e: At equilibrium: acid 2,8, alcohol 2,8, ester 1,2, water 1,2 mol. V cancels: Kc = 1,2² ÷ (2,8 × 2,8) = 0,184.

items.q: In the Haber process, N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ is exothermic. Why is a moderate temperature (about 450 °C) used?
c: a high temperature gives the best yield
a compromise between a good yield and a fast enough rate
items.e: A lower temperature gives more ammonia but the reaction would be too slow.

items.q: 5,0 mol of ethanoic acid and 1,0 mol of ethanol are mixed in 5,0 dm³. At equilibrium 0,80 mol of ethyl ethanoate has formed: CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH ⇌ CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O. Calculate K<sub>c</sub>.
items.e: At equilibrium: acid 4,2, alcohol 0,20, ester 0,80, water 0,80 mol. V cancels: Kc = 0,80² ÷ (4,2 × 0,20) = 0,762.

items.q: What is done with unreacted nitrogen and hydrogen in the Haber process?
c: it is released into the air
it is recycled back into the reactor
items.e: Recycling raises the overall yield.

items.q: Where does the hydrogen for the Haber process usually come from?
c: natural gas or coal (methane and steam)
items.e: In South Africa, Sasol makes hydrogen from coal.

items.q: Which South African company makes ammonia and fertilisers from coal at Sasolburg and Secunda?
items.e: Sasol uses coal to make hydrogen for ammonia.

items.q: 1,0 mol of ethanoic acid and 2,0 mol of ethanol are mixed in 5,0 dm³. At equilibrium 0,50 mol of ethyl ethanoate has formed: CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH ⇌ CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O. Calculate K<sub>c</sub>.
items.e: At equilibrium: acid 0,50, alcohol 1,5, ester 0,50, water 0,50 mol. V cancels: Kc = 0,50² ÷ (0,50 × 1,5) = 0,333.

items.q: 5,0 mol of ethanoic acid and 4,0 mol of ethanol are mixed in 2,0 dm³. At equilibrium 1,2 mol of ethyl ethanoate has formed: CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH ⇌ CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O. Calculate K<sub>c</sub>.
items.e: At equilibrium: acid 3,8, alcohol 2,8, ester 1,2, water 1,2 mol. V cancels: Kc = 1,2² ÷ (3,8 × 2,8) = 0,135.

items.q: Which industrial process makes ammonia?
items.e: N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃, with an iron catalyst.

items.q: 1,0 mol of ethanoic acid and 5,0 mol of ethanol are mixed in 1,0 dm³. At equilibrium 0,60 mol of ethyl ethanoate has formed: CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH ⇌ CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O. Calculate K<sub>c</sub>.
items.e: At equilibrium: acid 0,40, alcohol 4,4, ester 0,60, water 0,60 mol. V cancels: Kc = 0,60² ÷ (0,40 × 4,4) = 0,205.

items.q: What happens to the equilibrium CH<sub>4</sub> + H<sub>2</sub>O ⇌ CO + 3H<sub>2</sub> (all gases) if the pressure is increased?
c: the equilibrium shifts to the right
no change in the position of equilibrium
the equilibrium shifts to the left
items.e: There are 2 moles of gas on the left and 4 on the right. Higher pressure favours the side with fewer moles.

items.q: 5,0 mol of ethanoic acid and 3,0 mol of ethanol are mixed in 2,0 dm³. At equilibrium 0,60 mol of ethyl ethanoate has formed: CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH ⇌ CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O. Calculate K<sub>c</sub>.
items.e: At equilibrium: acid 4,4, alcohol 2,4, ester 0,60, water 0,60 mol. V cancels: Kc = 0,60² ÷ (4,4 × 2,4) = 0,0341.

items.q: 5,0 mol of ethanoic acid and 2,0 mol of ethanol are mixed in 2,0 dm³. At equilibrium 0,60 mol of ethyl ethanoate has formed: CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH ⇌ CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O. Calculate K<sub>c</sub>.
items.e: At equilibrium: acid 4,4, alcohol 1,4, ester 0,60, water 0,60 mol. V cancels: Kc = 0,60² ÷ (4,4 × 1,4) = 0,0584.

items.q: Where does the nitrogen for the Haber process come from?
c: the air (by fractional distillation of liquid air)
items.e: Air is about 78% nitrogen.

items.q: Which catalyst is used in the Haber process?
items.e: Finely divided iron speeds up the reaction.

items.q: 5,0 mol of ethanoic acid and 3,0 mol of ethanol are mixed in 1,0 dm³. At equilibrium 0,80 mol of ethyl ethanoate has formed: CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH ⇌ CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O. Calculate K<sub>c</sub>.
items.e: At equilibrium: acid 4,2, alcohol 2,2, ester 0,80, water 0,80 mol. V cancels: Kc = 0,80² ÷ (4,2 × 2,2) = 0,0693.

items.q: 5,0 mol of ethanoic acid and 2,0 mol of ethanol are mixed in 5,0 dm³. At equilibrium 1,2 mol of ethyl ethanoate has formed: CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH ⇌ CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O. Calculate K<sub>c</sub>.
items.e: At equilibrium: acid 3,8, alcohol 0,80, ester 1,2, water 1,2 mol. V cancels: Kc = 1,2² ÷ (3,8 × 0,80) = 0,474.

items.q: 5,0 mol of ethanoic acid and 3,0 mol of ethanol are mixed in 5,0 dm³. At equilibrium 1,2 mol of ethyl ethanoate has formed: CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH ⇌ CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O. Calculate K<sub>c</sub>.
items.e: At equilibrium: acid 3,8, alcohol 1,8, ester 1,2, water 1,2 mol. V cancels: Kc = 1,2² ÷ (3,8 × 1,8) = 0,211.

items.q: 3,0 mol of ethanoic acid and 1,0 mol of ethanol are mixed in 1,0 dm³. At equilibrium 0,50 mol of ethyl ethanoate has formed: CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH ⇌ CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O. Calculate K<sub>c</sub>.
items.e: At equilibrium: acid 2,5, alcohol 0,50, ester 0,50, water 0,50 mol. V cancels: Kc = 0,50² ÷ (2,5 × 0,50) = 0,200.

items.q: Why is a high pressure used in the Haber process?
c: high pressure stops the catalyst from working
the forward reaction makes fewer moles of gas, so high pressure favours ammonia
items.e: 4 mol of gas → 2 mol of gas; Le Chatelier's principle.

sets.title: Nitric acid, sulfuric acid and fertiliser salts

items.q: What is the first step of the Ostwald process?
items.e: Ammonia is oxidised to nitrogen monoxide.

items.q: What happens to the equilibrium CO + 2H<sub>2</sub> ⇌ CH<sub>3</sub>OH (all gases) if the pressure is increased?
c: the equilibrium shifts to the right
no change in the position of equilibrium
the equilibrium shifts to the left
items.e: There are 3 moles of gas on the left and 1 on the right. Higher pressure favours the side with fewer moles.

items.q: Ammonia reacts with sulfuric acid. Which fertiliser forms?
items.e: 2NH₃ + H₂SO₄ → (NH₄)₂SO₄.

items.q: In the contact process, SO₃ is dissolved in concentrated H₂SO₄, not in water. Why?
c: SO₃ and water react very exothermically and form a mist of acid
SO₃ does not react with water
items.e: SO₃ in H₂SO₄ gives oleum, H₂S₂O₇, which is then diluted.

items.q: In making sulfuric acid (contact process): 2SO<sub>2</sub> + O<sub>2</sub> ⇌ 2SO<sub>3</sub>, the energy change = −198 kJ. The pressure is decreased (the container is made larger). How does the equilibrium respond?
items.e: Left: 3 mol gas, right: 2 mol gas. Higher pressure favours fewer gas moles; lower pressure favours more.

items.q: In a lime kiln: CaCO<sub>3</sub>(s) ⇌ CaO(s) + CO<sub>2</sub>, the energy change = +178 kJ. The temperature is raised. How does the equilibrium respond?
items.e: the energy change = +178 kJ, so the forward reaction is endothermic. Heating favours the endothermic direction.

items.q: What happens to the equilibrium CO + H<sub>2</sub>O ⇌ CO<sub>2</sub> + H<sub>2</sub> (all gases) if the pressure is increased?
c: the equilibrium shifts to the right
the equilibrium shifts to the left
no change in the position of equilibrium
items.e: There are the same number of moles of gas on each side.

items.q: How is a phosphate fertiliser such as superphosphate made?
c: nitrogen is fixed from the air
phosphate rock is treated with sulfuric acid
items.e: Insoluble phosphate rock is made soluble with sulfuric acid.

items.q: Which industrial process makes nitric acid from ammonia?
items.e: Ammonia is oxidised to NO, then NO₂, which reacts with water to make HNO₃.

items.q: Which industrial process makes sulfuric acid?
items.e: SO₂ is oxidised to SO₃ over V₂O₅, then made into H₂SO₄.

items.q: Which catalyst is used in the contact process?
items.e: V₂O₅ catalyses 2SO₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2SO₃.

items.q: In a brown gas mixture: N<sub>2</sub>O<sub>4</sub> ⇌ 2NO<sub>2</sub>, the energy change = +57 kJ. The pressure is decreased (the container is made larger). How does the equilibrium respond?
items.e: Left: 1 mol gas, right: 2 mol gas. Higher pressure favours fewer gas moles; lower pressure favours more.

items.q: What does Le Chatelier's principle state?
c: equilibrium always lies to the right
a catalyst shifts equilibrium to the right
if a system at equilibrium is changed, the position of equilibrium shifts to partly oppose the change
items.e: It predicts the direction of shift.

items.q: What happens to the equilibrium N<sub>2</sub>O<sub>4</sub> ⇌ 2NO<sub>2</sub> (all gases) if the pressure is increased?
c: the equilibrium shifts to the left
the equilibrium shifts to the right
no change in the position of equilibrium
items.e: There are 1 moles of gas on the left and 2 on the right. Higher pressure favours the side with fewer moles.

items.q: In making methanol: CO + 2H<sub>2</sub> ⇌ CH<sub>3</sub>OH, the energy change = −91 kJ. Some CH<sub>3</sub>OH is removed. How does the equilibrium respond?
items.e: The system shifts to use up what was added or replace what was removed.

items.q: For N<sub>2</sub>O<sub>4</sub> ⇌ 2NO<sub>2</sub>, the energy change = 58 kJ mol⁻¹. What happens if the temperature is decreased?
c: the equilibrium shifts to the right and K<sub>c</sub> increases
the equilibrium shifts to the left and K<sub>c</sub> decreases
the equilibrium shifts to the right but K<sub>c</sub> stays the same
items.e: The forward reaction is endothermic. Cooling favours the exothermic direction. Only temperature changes K<sub>c</sub>.

items.q: Which catalyst is used in the Ostwald process?
items.e: Ammonia is oxidised to NO over a platinum gauze.

items.q: In a brown gas mixture: N<sub>2</sub>O<sub>4</sub> ⇌ 2NO<sub>2</sub>, the energy change = +57 kJ. The temperature is raised. How does the equilibrium respond?
items.e: the energy change = +57 kJ, so the forward reaction is endothermic. Heating favours the endothermic direction.

items.q: What happens to the equilibrium N<sub>2</sub> + 3H<sub>2</sub> ⇌ 2NH<sub>3</sub> (all gases) if the pressure is increased?
c: no change in the position of equilibrium
the equilibrium shifts to the right
the equilibrium shifts to the left
items.e: There are 4 moles of gas on the left and 2 on the right. Higher pressure favours the side with fewer moles.

items.q: In a closed flask of PCl₅: PCl<sub>5</sub> ⇌ PCl<sub>3</sub> + Cl<sub>2</sub>, the energy change = +88 kJ. A catalyst is added. How does the equilibrium respond?
items.e: A catalyst speeds up both directions equally, so it does not shift equilibrium.

items.q: 1,0 mol of ethanoic acid and 5,0 mol of ethanol are mixed in 5,0 dm³. At equilibrium 0,50 mol of ethyl ethanoate has formed: CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH ⇌ CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O. Calculate K<sub>c</sub>.
items.e: At equilibrium: acid 0,50, alcohol 4,5, ester 0,50, water 0,50 mol. V cancels: Kc = 0,50² ÷ (0,50 × 4,5) = 0,111.

items.q: 4,0 mol of ethanoic acid and 5,0 mol of ethanol are mixed in 2,0 dm³. At equilibrium 1,5 mol of ethyl ethanoate has formed: CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH ⇌ CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O. Calculate K<sub>c</sub>.
items.e: At equilibrium: acid 2,5, alcohol 3,5, ester 1,5, water 1,5 mol. V cancels: Kc = 1,5² ÷ (2,5 × 3,5) = 0,257.

items.q: In a sealed tube of hydrogen and iodine: H<sub>2</sub> + I<sub>2</sub> ⇌ 2HI, the energy change = −9 kJ. Some HI is removed. How does the equilibrium respond?
items.e: The system shifts to use up what was added or replace what was removed.

items.q: 3,0 mol of ethanoic acid and 2,0 mol of ethanol are mixed in 5,0 dm³. At equilibrium 0,60 mol of ethyl ethanoate has formed: CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH ⇌ CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O. Calculate K<sub>c</sub>.
items.e: At equilibrium: acid 2,4, alcohol 1,4, ester 0,60, water 0,60 mol. V cancels: Kc = 0,60² ÷ (2,4 × 1,4) = 0,107.

items.q: In making sulfuric acid (contact process): 2SO<sub>2</sub> + O<sub>2</sub> ⇌ 2SO<sub>3</sub>, the energy change = −198 kJ. The temperature is raised. How does the equilibrium respond?
items.e: the energy change = −198 kJ, so the forward reaction is exothermic. Heating favours the endothermic direction.

items.q: 1,0 mol of ethanoic acid and 3,0 mol of ethanol are mixed in 2,0 dm³. At equilibrium 0,80 mol of ethyl ethanoate has formed: CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH ⇌ CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O. Calculate K<sub>c</sub>.
items.e: At equilibrium: acid 0,20, alcohol 2,2, ester 0,80, water 0,80 mol. V cancels: Kc = 0,80² ÷ (0,20 × 2,2) = 1,45.
